section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1970
title: 8 TABLE III— The variations in the incidence of accidental deaths in the different regions result from a large number of factors peculiar to the region such as the topography of the area, the population, the level of industrialisation and other socio-economic factors. Considering population as one of the major concomitant variants, the volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population in the different States and Union Territories and Cities has been estimated and presented in Table IV. The highest number of accidental deaths occurred in the State of Maharashtra (24944) followed by Uttar Pradesh (19915), Madhya Pradesh (18207) and West Bengal (12436). These four States together accounted for 54% of total accidental deaths in the entire country. The volume of accidental deaths per one lakh of population was also the highest in Maharashtra (49.7), followed by Madhya Pradesh (44.6), Orissa (35.7), Gujarat (29.1) and West Bengal (27.7) against an average of 25.3 for all the States together. The volume of accidental deaths is consistently higher in all the Union Territories, except Laccadives, the average being 40.1% for all the Union Territories together. Among the Cities, the highest volume of accidental deaths was noticed in Bombay (107.7) and the lowest in Calcutta (12.3) against an average of 53.8 for all the Cities under study together.
